description:
The most important piece of your AI stack might be the one thing you never wrote a line of code for. This is the AI gateway (also called an LLM gateway): the layer that sits between your app and every model you call, and the reason a "cheaper" model can end up costing you more.

In this video: what an AI gateway actually does, why almost every team ends up building one by accident, the real difference between an AI gateway, an LLM gateway, an API gateway, an MCP gateway, and an inference gateway, and the routing trade-off that can turn a cost-saving move into a bigger bill.

What is an AI gateway?
An AI gateway (sometimes called an LLM gateway) is the shared layer that sits between your application and the model providers you call: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and the rest. Instead of every service holding its own API keys and writing its own retry logic, the gateway centralizes five things: a single unified API across providers, key management, automatic retries and failover, token and cost tracking, and observability. It's an old idea (the API gateway) applied to model traffic. Most teams don't start with one. They back into it once a second provider, a second internal service, or the first surprise invoice forces the question.

This video also covers:
- The difference between rule-based routing and smart/semantic routing
- Why RouteLLM-style routers can hold most of a frontier model's quality while sending a fraction of requests its way
- The cache-aware routing trade-off: why switching to a "cheaper" model mid-session can cost more once you count the cold cache reload
- Semantic caching: how it works, and how a similarity threshold set too loose serves the wrong answer
- When you actually need a gateway, and when calling a model directly is the right call
